(a) EXACT THEORY: Theorem A (orbit structure) re-derived by hand (action law (b,c,d)->(lam*b, 2b*al+c, lam^{-1}(b*al^2+(c+1)*al+d)) confirmed on 300 random flint compositions) and exhaustively re-verified for p=3..13 with my own code, including the b=0 stratum being exactly {x^p-x+d, d!=0}; counts 8/24/48/120/324 reproduced. Theorem C (quantization T_u = eta(-1)G_Q(R(u)-1)) — the double-evaluation proof is correct (Q/G_Q = eta(-1)G_Q since G_Q*conj(G_Q)=Q, conj(G_Q)=eta(-1)G_Q) and I confirmed it exhaustively for every u at p=3,5 with independent code; the p=3 Salié cross-check values (T_1=0, T_2=-2G_Q, S(3)=-G_Q) match my run. Lemma L1 proof correct, verified p<5000. Theorem D equivalences follow immediately. DATA: my own no-prefilter full-Rabin implementation (compose_mod doubling, validated against flint factor() on 240 random polynomials) plus a flint-free sympy cross-check (p=13,19,31) reproduced N(p) and the exact witness d-lists at p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,101 and 5 random table primes 263,587,887,919,1153 — all match. The two teams' N tables agree perfectly on all 195 common primes including d-lists. The task's 'Poisson mean ~1 -> 1/e zeros' benchmark is REJECTED by the data: Poisson(1) predicts 87.6 zeros vs 61 observed (-3.6 sigma). The correct naive benchmark is the rootless-conditioned mean e/2~1.359 (only (p-1)/2 values of d lack F_p-roots, each irreducible with conditional probability ~e/p); Poisson(e/2) predicts P(0)=0.257 vs observed 0.256 — striking — yet the observed MEAN 1.181 sits 2.8 sigma below e/2, and relative to Poisson(observed mean) there is a zero deficit (-1.7 sigma) plus underdispersion.
